eligibility.summary: Eligibility for this program is statutorily limited (Section 546 of the Public Health Service Act [42 USC 290ee-1], as amended) to states, local governmental entities, and Indian Tribes and Tribal organizations (as defined in section 4 of the Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act). In North Carolina, eligible entities fitting the organizational requirements may apply.

cost_share.details: Non-federal cost sharing or matching is required under this program.

review_criteria.criterion: Work Plan Feasibility and Milestone Schedule

submission_limits: Institutional limits apply as detailed in the opportunity announcement; verify internal screening procedures.
important_notes: Opportunity Number: TI-27-006 — Agency: Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Adminis.
Forecasted Opportunity: This is an advance forecast notice. Official application packages and final closing dates will be released upon posting.
Application submission is administered via Grants.gov or the designated federal portal for opportunity TI-27-006.
SAM.gov registration must be active with valid Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) prior to submission; allow 3-4 weeks for new registrations.
Review all instructions, eligibility requirements, and deadlines published on Grants.gov before preparing submission.

funded_activities.activity: Eligible activities supporting First Responders-Comprehensive Addiction and Recovery Act: The purpose of this program is to train first responders and communities in administering and distributing opioid overdose reversal medications (OORM).
